hard_nevers: Never push to remote without explicit approval, even with green CI
Never block on the configuration provider's first load
Never let the React UI reach the database directly
Never write to a scope outside the configured scopeFilter from the same host
Never refactor mutation audit writes to fire-and-forget
failure_modes: Citing warp types (WarpWorkerService, JobCommandService, InterceptorConstants) that do not exist in db-config
Assuming net8.0 only when packages multi-target net8.0;net10.0
Running dotnet test and trusting exit code 5 instead of invoking the test executable
invisible_conventions: TenantId empty string is the global-default sentinel, not NULL
All four scope columns use case-sensitive collation
Tenant fallback lives in DbConfigConfigurationProvider.TryGet, never in the store layer
Audit Action reflects the DB state transition at SaveChangesAsync, not caller intent
answers.branch_pr_workflow: Hierarchical branches with / (feat/, fix/, chore/, docs/, test/, bug/). Conventional-commit prefixes in recent history (feat:, fix:, test:, chore:, refactor:) alongside vX.Y.Z release headers. PRs merged via GitHub UI after review; assign @me.
compliance_constraints: Mutation audit rows must commit in the same SaveChangesAsync as the mutation
Read audits are fire-and-forget by design (documented exception)
IsSecret values encrypted at rest; audit old/new values carry the same ciphertext form
done_definition: dotnet build clean with zero warnings (TreatWarningsAsErrors=true)
Tests green on BOTH SQL Server and PostgreSQL via Testcontainers
Tests run by invoking the test executable directly, not dotnet test (MTP runner exit-5 quirk)
Docs/website updated when public API or behavior changes
answers.product_purpose: A database-backed IConfiguration provider for .NET with an embedded React editor UI, letting teams change application configuration at runtime without a redeploy.
